classification.difficultyReason: Interpret compass arcs as equal radii and follow the specified SSS-to-SAS proof chain. Transfer the first angle equality to the smaller triangles, then combine equal adjacent angles with a straight angle to prove perpendicularity.

content.prompt: This question provides a proof of the construction of the perpendicular from a given point to a given line.

spec.description: Horizontal line through A, M and B; F above M; solid FM; supplied right-angle square at M; dashed vertical continuation through G. A compass arc centred at F passes through A and B, and equal-radius lower arcs centred at A and B intersect at G.
spec.mathematics: FA=FB as radii of the first circle; AG=BG from the equal-radius construction arcs. F, M and G are collinear. The source supplies a right-angle marker although perpendicularity is subsequently requested as a proof.
spec.answerVisibility: Only printed construction marks are supplied. AF, BF, AG and BG are left for the student to join.

answer.worked:
$FA=FB$ because they are radii of the circle centred at $F$.

$AG=BG$ because the construction arcs centred at $A$ and $B$ have equal radii.

$FG=FG$ is a common side.

Therefore $\triangle AFG\equiv\triangle BFG$ (SSS).

answer.short: $\angle AFG=\angle BFG$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).
answer.worked: From (b), $\triangle AFG\equiv\triangle BFG$. Hence $\angle AFG=\angle BFG$ because matching angles of congruent triangles are equal.

answer.short: $\triangle AFM\equiv\triangle BFM$ (SAS): $FA=FB$, $\angle AFM=\angle BFM$ and $FM$ is common.

answer.short:
$\angle AMF=\angle BMF=90^\circ$, so $FG\perp AB$.

The angles are equal by congruence and sum to $180^\circ$ on the straight line $AB$.
answer.worked:
From (d), $\angle AMF=\angle BMF$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).

Since $A$, $M$ and $B$ lie on a straight line,
$$\angle AMF+\angle BMF=180^\circ.$$
Therefore $\angle AMF=\angle BMF=90^\circ$.

As $F$, $M$ and $G$ are collinear, $FG\perp AB$.
